aptu-coder

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) code-intelligence server that gives AI coding agents pre-parsed symbol tables instead of raw file bytes, cutting token usage by up to 59% in the cited benchmark conditions (see Benchmarks). OpenSSF silver certified: fewer than 1% of open source projects reach this level.

> [!NOTE] > Native agent tools (regex search, path matching, file reading) handle targeted lookups well. `aptu-coder` handles the mechanical, non-AI work: mapping directory structure and extracting symbols, so a coding agent's context window is spent reasoning instead of re-deriving structure on every call. Most code-intelligence tooling for AI agents indexes a codebase into a cloud embedding or vector store and retrieves by similarity search. aptu-coder instead parses the codebase on-device with tree-sitter and serves it locally over MCP: no source code leaves the machine, and retrieval is exact (symbol tables) rather than approximate (nearest-neighbor similarity). ## Benchmarks Paired comprehension tasks on Claude Code (MCP mode vs native shell search). Methodology: [Django](https://github.com/django/django) auth migration ([v12](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v12/methodology.md)) and [OpenFAST](https://github.com/OpenFAST/openfast) AeroDyn integration audit ([v13](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v13/methodology.md)). | Task | Mode | Sonnet 4.6 | Haiku 4.5 | Savings | |---|---|---|---|---| | Django (Python) | MCP | 112k tokens, $0.39 | 406k tokens, $0.42 | **59% fewer tokens, 59% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | Django (Python) | Native | 276k tokens, $0.95 | 473k tokens, $0.53 | 14% fewer tokens, 21% cheaper (Haiku) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | MCP | 472k tokens, $1.65 | 687k tokens, $0.72 | **46% fewer tokens, 42% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | Native | 877k tokens, $2.85 | 2162k tokens, $2.21 | **68% fewer tokens, 68% cheaper** (Haiku) | A real end-to-end multi-agent run against this repository itself: five refactoring issues (#1578–#1582) fixed by the [coder skill](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill) in one orchestrated session — 23 subagent spawns (5 scout, 1 guard, 10 build, 7 check), ~1h42m, three human interventions — producing PRs #1584–#1588, all merged with CI green. [Case study](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill/blob/main/docs/examples/2026-09-aptu-coder-5-issues.md). ### Scope of the benchmark claims The token-savings figures above come from single, focused comprehension tasks where the agent used aptu-coder instead of shell search. Agentic coding loops have bash and ripgrep and can search the repo directly. The [v19 benchmark program](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/audit/2026-09-30-v19-pivot.md) (N=20 paired sessions, pre-registered claim gate) measured aptu-coder in those loops: no measurable answer-quality gain over bash + ripgrep on structural fan-in tasks (pooled paired F1 diff mean -0.071, 95% CI [-0.179, +0.038]; gate NOT-SUPPORTED); tool activation itself was reliable when tools were surfaced directly. - PHP is one of the most widely deployed server-side languages and is absent from the registry: no `php` in `EXTENSION_MAP` (`crates/aptu-coder-core/src/lang.rs`), no handler in `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/`, no `tree-sitter-php` in `Cargo.lock`.

## Prerequisites

None.

## Where to Look

- **Handler templates:** `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/java.rs` (an OO language with `extends` / `implements`) and `swift.rs` (inheritance through named children, inline tests).
- **Grammar:** the `tree-sitter-php` repository on GitHub. Node kinds and field names come from `php/src/node-types.json`; the crate entry points are on docs.rs.
- **Registry:** `languages/mod.rs` (handler registration) and `lang.rs` (extension map and supported-language list).

## Scope

- A new handler, `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs`, with the SPDX header and the five query constants used by the other handlers (`ELEMENT_QUERY`, `CALL_QUERY`, `REFERENCE_QUERY`, `IMPORT_QUERY`, `DEFUSE_QUERY`).

- Registry wiring for `"php"` in both `languages/mod.rs` and `lang.rs`.
- Unit tests in `php.rs` and one integration test file under `crates/aptu-coder/tests/`.
- `README.md`: add PHP to the Supported Languages list and the intro count.

1. Pick the crate version from crates.io and check it against the workspace `tree-sitter` version.
2. Parse a small sample `.php` file with the grammar and list the node kinds and fields you see. Confirm each one in `php/src/node-types.json` before you use it.
3. Write the five queries and prove they compile in a unit test before wiring anything. The tree-sitter query syntax documentation covers captures and fields.
4. Mirror the registry wiring of the most recent language addition.
5. Add the unit tests and the integration test last.

Expect a day or two of work; most of it is step 2.

- [ ] `extract_inheritance` on `class Foo extends Bar implements A, B` returns `["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]`; on a class with no clauses it returns `[]`

- [ ] An integration test covers one happy path and the HTML-template edge case, using `common::call_tool_raw` and `tempfile::NamedTempFile` as in `tests/integration_tests.rs`

- [ ] Commits are GPG signed and DCO signed off

- Trait `use` resolution, property and constant extraction, attributes, namespace import aliasing
- `.phtml`, `.inc`, `.module`, `.php5` extensions
- Tool handler or schema changes; other languages

The maintainers are implementing this in-house. External pull requests for this issue are not being accepted at this time and will be closed.

## Related

- #648 and #1742: the Swift integration, the most recent language addition
- #1063: binary size delta reporting

### base_clause and class_interface_clause rules

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js

The rules that carry out the role of the queried parent_class/base_classes/interfaces: base_clause matches 'extends' followed by names, and class_interface_clause matches 'implements' followed by names. Neither field name exists as a class_declaration field.

```javascript
      base_clause: $ => seq(
        keyword('extends'),
        commaSep1($._name),
      ),

// ...

      class_interface_clause: $ => seq(
        keyword('implements'),
        commaSep1($._name),
      ),
```

--------------------------------

### class_declaration rule definition

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js

The grammar rule for class_declaration: it defines the field 'name' (plus 'attributes' and 'body'), and uses optional base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) nodes instead of parent_class/base_classes/interfaces fields. Method declarations appear inside the body's declaration_list, and functions are named function_definition in this grammar.

```javascript
      class_declaration: $ => prec.right(seq(
        optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)),
        repeat($._modifier),
        keyword('class'),
        field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)),
        optional($.base_clause),
        optional($.class_interface_clause),
        field('body', $.declaration_list),
      )),
```

--------------------------------

### Anonymous class variations with constructor, inheritance, and traits

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/test/corpus/class.txt

Shows multiple anonymous class instantiations: with a method, with extends and implements, with a property, with constructor arguments and a trait, and nested inside a class method returning an anonymous class with a constant. The parse tree covers all these forms.

```php
new class {
    public function test() {}
};
new class extends A implements B, C {};
new class() {
    public $foo;
};
new class($a, $b) extends A {
    use T;
};

class A {
    public function test() {
        return new class($this) extends A {
            const A = 'B';
        };
    }
}
```

The Scout output is written to `exp5-output.json` and parses as valid JSON. Start time was 2026-11-28T01:03:27Z, finish 2026-11-28T01:06:25Z (178 s).

## Key findings

- **The tree-sitter-php grammar has no `superclass` or `interfaces` fields.** `class_declaration` only has `name`, `body` and `attributes`. `extends` and `implements` sit in unfielded `base_clause` and `class_interface_clause` children. Java's field-based `extract_inheritance` cannot be copied; PHP needs a child walk.
- **`DEFUSE_QUERY` is required.** `parser_elements.rs` returns an empty vector when `defuse` is `None`, so PHP would return no definition or use sites without it.
- **`"php"` must be in `supported_languages()`.** `parser.rs` builds `QUERY_CACHE` from that list. `css` is absent from it, so the css integration is not a complete template.
- **Use `LANGUAGE_PHP`, not `LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY`.** The acceptance criteria need a mixed HTML/PHP file to parse without ERROR nodes.
- **`tree-sitter-language` 0.1.9 is already in `Cargo.lock`.** Only the `tree-sitter-php` entry is new.
- **Grammar version:** tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 is the latest GitHub release. Its `Cargo.toml`, `common/define-grammar.js` and `php/src/node-types.json` were fetched and checked against every node kind used.

## Recommendation

Approach A: a full `php.rs` modeled on `java.rs`, with all five queries, a child-walk `extract_inheritance`, and registry wiring in `lang.rs` and `languages/mod.rs`. It is the only option that meets the issue's acceptance criteria. Approach B (no defuse or inheritance) is simpler but fails them. Approach C (reuse the grammar's `tags.scm`) is listed but unverified.

## Caveats

- I did not run `cargo build` or `cargo test`, so the queries are validated only against `node-types.json` and the grammar rules, not by compiling.
- `message_count` (26) is my estimate of the number of turns, not a counted value.
- Line ranges for `java.rs` and `ELEMENT_QUERY` or `DEFUSE_QUERY` in other files are approximate. The `mod.rs`, `lang.rs` and `parser_elements.rs` ranges were confirmed with `rg`.
